title: Compact generators and finite-Tor constructible compactness on finite-type etale sites without separatedness
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $C$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. No separatedness of $T$ over $k$ is assumed. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and standard cohomology [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Call $E$ bounded constructible if $H^i(E)=0$ for all but finitely many $i$ and each $H^i(E)$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Say $E$ has finite Tor amplitude if there are integers $r\le s$ such that for every sheaf $N$ of $C$-modules placed in degree zero, $H^i(E\otimes_C^L N)=0$ for every $i\notin[r,s]$.

Every bounded constructible complex of finite Tor amplitude is compact [def-pc-compact-object] in $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$. There exist a set $S$ in the indexing universe and a family $(E_s)_{s\in S}$ of bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude such that, for every morphism $h:A\to B$ in $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, if postcomposition $\operatorname{Hom}(E_s[n],A)\to\operatorname{Hom}(E_s[n],B)$ is bijective for all $s\in S$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, then $h$ is an isomorphism. The category has arbitrary set-indexed coproducts and is locally small in the corresponding Hom universe.

The section assumes qcqs, not separatedness; finite-type schemes here are Noetherian and qcqs.

proof.text: A locally finite-type scheme over Spec k is locally Noetherian. Quasi-compactness of its structure map gives CompactSpace T, hence IsNoetherian T. ModuleCat-valued etale sheaves form a Grothendieck abelian category. The existing derived-category instance gives local smallness in u+1. Apply the general derived_hasCoproducts theorem to get coproducts indexed in u+1; no termwise coproduct comparison is required here.

proof.text: Let P be compact objects. compactObjects_isThick makes P triangulated, retract closed and isomorphism closed. Apply etaleThickGeneration from the Noetherian complement of sk-lem-sf-flat-model. Each generator is a single complex of the ordinary closed pushforward of the open extension of a finite locally constant flat sheaf. A flat sheaf has flat geometric fibres: use the existing source Point.flat_sheafFiber_obj after lifting the point to universe u+1, and transfer back using uliftSheafFiberIso. The stratum compactness theorem applies to exactly this object. Transport along its specified isomorphism. Thick generation therefore proves compactness of every bounded constructible finite-Tor object.

proof.text: Take S=T.AffineEtale, a type in u+1, and E_U=affineEtaleFreeComplex C T U. This is the explicit free Yoneda sheaf placed in degree zero. The proved source isConstructibleSheaf_freeYoneda is the affine Noetherian specialization of free-etale-sheaf constructibility; boundedConstructible_singleFunctor_obj gives its cohomological constructibility, which is transported through isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff. The standard t-structure shows its cohomology vanishes outside [0,0]. The proved source flat_freeYoneda specializes free_sheaf_flat to C. Its single complex is bounded and termwise flat, including the zero terms. Apply hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flatModel to conclude Tor amplitude [0,0].

split_report.summary: Preserved every hypothesis and conclusion, including nonseparated T, arbitrary algebraically closed k and unbounded targets. Split finite-Tor compactness through the existing Noetherian finite-ring flat-model devissage and a smaller lisse-stratum compactness input; constructed a small affine-etale family and proved its morphism detection via natural K-injective section-Hom formulas and local cocycle/boundary arguments. Added one statement-only Bhatt–Scholze input; searched project Lean, whole DAG, current blueprint and Mathlib, twice by concept. No SGA route, Lean edits or builds. Retry audit: made the small-site universe convention explicit and removed the redundant free-extension compactness node, since step 3 already proves compactness of the finite-Tor free generators constructed in step 4.
split_report.blueprint: Adic-stage paragraph: "For Λ in {O_E,E,Qlb}, use respectively derived inverse limits, rationalization, and the common-stage construction ... of the compatible finite-level functors"; finite-level compact generators used to control coproducts of coefficient-system adjoints. Steps 1–3 give finite-Tor compactness; steps 4–6 give the compact generator family, size and detection needed by the finite-stage right-adjoint coproduct argument.
